baseline.note: One System transfer per recipient does the same work.
Two transfers with client-computed amounts settle the same way, but nothing on chain ties the two amounts to one total or bounds the share.
Transfers with client-computed weights settle the same way; the weighting rule itself is not enforced on chain.
A bare transfer refunds unconditionally; the deadline is only checked by whoever builds the transaction.
A transfer of a client-computed amount can be built, but no on-chain check proves the reserve survived.
ATA CreateIdempotent then Transfer per recipient. The ATA program derives the address itself, so the guarantee matches.
One SPL Token transfer per destination does the same work.
ATA CreateIdempotent is the same behavior in one instruction.
CloseAccount per candidate works only while every candidate is empty: SPL Token rejects a funded account, which fails the whole transaction instead of skipping that row.
A bare transfer moves the tokens; nothing proves the source was debited by exactly that amount and no more.
The route instruction alone. Deadline and minimum output are whatever the client checked before signing.
The same instruction with no schema: a substituted program ID or a wrong-owner account is accepted as far as the transaction is concerned.
No instruction sequence reads an oracle account and refuses to continue. Enforcing a band on chain needs a program.
A transaction cannot compare a balance before and after one of its own instructions. Capping the debit on chain needs a program.
A transaction cannot derive a PDA and compare it to a supplied account. Rejecting a substituted account on chain needs a program.
Both instructions can be sent back to back, but the intermediate token delta is never checked, so a bad fill still deposits.
A claim instruction followed by one token transfer per recipient does the same work.
The client picks a route and sends that one instruction. The choice is made before signing, not from state at execution time.
A transaction cannot read a proposal flag and a timestamp and refuse to execute. Gating on chain needs a program.
One crank instruction per row does the same work.
